clusters.title: Trump’s vaccine order is about feelings, not facts | Robert B Shpiner
clusters.neutral_headline: Trump’s vaccine order is about feelings, not facts | Robert B Shpiner

items.title: Trump’s vaccine order is about feelings, not facts | Robert B Shpiner
items.standfirst: There’s no evidence that vaccines cause autism, or that we should separate MMR shots. This order is dangerous“This is based on what I feel.” That was the president last September, explaining why he wanted the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine broken into three separate shots. On Monday, he signed an executive order instructing exactly that.Four decades in intensive care have taught me what a feeling costs once it becomes national policy. Children will be hospitalized who did not need to be. Some of them will die. No one can name those the vaccine has saved, because prevented harm is invisible by definition, and that invisibility is what makes preventive medicine easy to dismantle and hard to defend. Continue reading...

clusters.title: ‘I’m giving people a happy space’: the man clearing gardens for free – and letting light into strangers’ lives
clusters.neutral_headline: ‘I’m giving people a happy space’: the man clearing gardens for free –...

items.title: ‘I’m giving people a happy space’: the man clearing gardens for free – and letting light into strangers’ lives
items.standfirst: When he saw a messy yard being criticised on social media, Stephen Jalland grabbed his trimmer and decided to help. An overgrown garden, he discovered, often hides an overwhelmed ownerAnita Thursby had been dreading the gas engineer coming to service her boiler. They would have needed to enter her kitchen, where the window looked into the jungle of swirling, 2-metre-high brambles that made up her back garden, and her shame had spiralled. “I would have been horrified,” she says. For the same reason, the 54-year-old had stopped inviting friends over to her house and had been living in fear of a complaint from her housing association.Maintaining the garden had slipped from her grasp, becoming a source of constant worry, yet pride had stopped her asking for help – and tight finances from paying for it. Family barbecues had become a distant memory, even though she longed to have her 83-year-old mother round to sit in the sun; weeks ago, she bought a grill in Tesco with little hope of ever using it. Continue reading...

clusters.title: ‘Drops take seconds but change a life for ever’: the women saving India’s remotest people from polio
clusters.neutral_headline: ‘Drops take seconds but change a life for ever’: the women...

items.title: ‘Drops take seconds but change a life for ever’: the women saving India’s remotest people from polio
items.standfirst: Shameema and Tanzeela must trek for miles in summer heat to vaccinate children in Kashmir’s highlands as part of a vast national programmeBefore sunrise, Shameema slips on her worn rubber sandals and checks the insulated box – the ice packs inside must maintain the crucial cold chain at between 2C and 8C (35.6-46.4F). She hoists the container on one shoulder and steps out into the dark.Tanzeela follows with her own pack, after quickly retying the laces of her canvas shoes. Both women live in Pulwama, a district where summer temperatures climb to 37C. Their destination lies higher, out of the valley where asphalt turns to dirt track and then to a barely distinguishable footpath along the floor of the mountain pine forests. Continue reading...
